definitions.explanation: An area far from the center of civilization, often near national borders or in sparsely populated territory.

examples.japanese: {辺境|へんきょう}の{村|むら}を{訪|おとず}れた。
examples.english: I visited a village in a remote region.

examples.japanese: {辺境|へんきょう}の{地|ち}では{医療|いりょう}サービスが{不足|ふそく}している。
examples.english: Medical services are lacking in frontier regions.

examples.japanese: かつてローマ{帝国|ていこく}の{辺境|へんきょう}だったこの{地域|ちいき}には、{今|いま}も{古代|こだい}の{要塞|ようさい}の{跡|あと}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: In this region, once on the frontier of the Roman Empire, ruins of ancient fortresses still remain.

notes:
Compound of {辺|へん} (periphery, edge) + {境|きょう} (border, boundary).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {辺境|へんきょう}の{地|ち} (a remote land)
- {辺境|へんきょう}の{村|むら} (a frontier village)
- {辺境|へんきょう}を{守|まも}る (to defend the frontier)
- {辺境|へんきょう}{伯|はく} (margrave — a feudal title)

USAGE:
Often used in historical, geographical, and fantasy contexts. In fantasy fiction, {辺境|へんきょう} frequently describes the remote edges of a kingdom. The term carries a sense of distance from power and civilization.
